newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Burton set for strong 1st half.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Burton set for strong 1st half.

text.p: British retailer Burton Group Plc will have to show if it can keep up last year's impressive performance when it reports first half results next Thursday.

Britain's second biggest clothing retailer, owner of Debenhams, Dorothy Perkins and Top Shop, is forecast to report a healthy increase in half year pretax profits to between 105 and 110 million stg, from 88.1 million a year ago. Analysts are forecasting a dividend of about 1.35 pence, against 1.15.
The group achieved a major turnaround in margins last year, but now investors want to see if there is scope for further growth.
"Last time they got everything moving in the right direction, the question now is can they pull it off for two sets of results in a row," said one retail analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Last November, when the company reported a 54 percent increase in full year profits, Burton said there was scope for further improvement in gross margins, but at a slower pace.
This time analysts are also looking for sales growth, given that there may be more limited scope for further margin gains.
"They need to show they can drive sales growth," said another retail analyst.
In January Burton reported that sales in the 20 weeks to January 18 were up 11.1 percent, with Debenhams department store up 9.1 percent and its multiples (clothing stores) up 5.4 percent.

Analysts said the market wanted some reassurance that the womenswear multiples were taking full advantage of the buoyant conditions in the clothing retail market and were holding their ground against competitors such as Next Plc.
There is also interest in what Burton is doing to improve its menswear business, which has lagged behind the rest of the group's recovery.

Last year Burton joined the growing number of retailers moving into mail order via the purchase of Innovations and Racing Green, and there should be an update on how these new businesses are performing.
The shares, which climbed strongly early this year to a peak of 163 pence, are currently below the highs. They were unchanged at 153-1/2 pence by 0735 GMT.
